tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Check the Callman connection: server URL, the user the token acts as, token permissions (scopes), the workspaces you can use (and which one is the default), enabled features and which tools are available with this token. Call this first in a session, or when a tool reports a permission problem.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces you belong to, with your role in each (owner / editor / viewer) and which one is the session default. The token works in all of them; a token keeps your role: writes are refused where you are a viewer.

tools.name: use_workspace
tools.description: Pick the workspace new things go to for the rest of this session (collections, environments, scenarios, imports — anything created without `workspace`), and the one that wins when a name exists in several workspaces. It never hides the others: lists and searches still cover every workspace. `workspace: null` clears the default. Lasts until the MCP server restarts; CALLMAN_WORKSPACE_ID sets it at start.

tools.name: add_workspace_member
tools.description: Add a person to a workspace by email with a role (editor can write collections/requests/scenarios; viewer is read-only; owner manages the workspace). Turn the user's request into routes: each route is { method, path, response } — response is static ({ type: "static", statusCode, headers?, body }), template ({{request.params.id}}, {{faker.email}}, {{state.key}} …) or builder (list/detail/create/update/delete over the mock's state). tools.name: run_load_test
tools.description:
Generate load against the requests of a collection from THIS machine and judge it against pass criteria. Same engine as the desktop's Load test and `callme perf run`. The requests of the collection (or one folder, or the ones named in `only`) run in order as one flow per iteration, with the environment's variables.
Two steps: without `confirm: true` it only PREVIEWS (target hosts, requests, planned traffic, limits) — show that to the user, then call again with confirm: true. Only test systems the user owns or may load-test.
Pattern: `mode: "vus"` (a closed crowd of virtual users looping the flow; slow servers slow them down) or `mode: "rate"` (an open model: iterations START at `rate` per second whatever the server does; iterations that cannot start are reported as dropped). `rampUpSeconds` ramps to the level first. Or pick a `preset` (smoke, load, stress, spike, breakpoint) tuned by vus / rate / durationSeconds.
Pass criteria: `thresholds` like "p95<500", "fail<1%", "checks>99%", "rps>100" or "http_req_duration{step:Login}:p(95)<300"; `abortOn` takes the same but stops the run when one breaks (use it to find the breaking point).
Returns the verdict, throughput, latency percentiles, failures by cause (and whether the load generator or the target is to blame), per-step numbers and threshold results. Scripts, DB and Redis steps are not run. Limits here: 200 users, 500 iterations/s, 120 s per run. Needs requests:run.

instructions:
Callman is an API client and test platform: collections of HTTP requests, environments with variables, multi-step API test scenarios, UI tests (web / Android / iOS flows), mock APIs, and system-design diagrams. You act as the user whose token is configured, within that token's permissions and the user's workspace role.
Start with whoami. The token works in every workspace the user belongs to: lists and searches cover all of them unless you pass `workspace`, names are looked up in the default workspace first and then everywhere, and results say which workspace they come from; creating something needs a target (`workspace`, the collection it goes into, or the session default — use_workspace). Names work as references (collection, folder, request, environment, scenario, UI test, diagram, workspace); ambiguous names return candidates. List before creating — duplicate collection names are refused. Preview large writes with dryRun: true; deletions need confirm: true and the user's agreement. Environment values are masked unless the token holds environments:reveal and you pass reveal: true; never write a masked value back. Arguments are strict — an unknown key is an error listing the valid ones. Read callman://docs/overview for the conventions, callman://docs/request-schema before creating or editing requests, callman://docs/contracts before contract checks, callman://docs/scenario-nodes before scenarios, callman://docs/ui-tests (+ callman://docs/ui-test-steps) before UI tests — they run on the server runner (web) or the user's own desktop app (list_ui_test_devices), callman://docs/mocks before mock APIs (create_mock: a public URL on the server, or target: "desktop" for a local mock in the user's desktop app), and callman://docs/diagram-schema + callman://diagram/components before diagrams.
